privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.intro: Tandem is a private, non-commercial app used by the members of a household to organise their tasks. This page explains what data it processes, why, and how to delete it.

who.title: Who manages your data
who.body: The app is hosted and run by a member of the household, on their own server (behind Cloudflare). There are no ads, no data sales and no tracking: your data is only used to run the app for your household.

data.title: Data processed
data.body:
Account: first name, email address, password (only as an Argon2 hash, never in clear text), language.
Household: household name, members, categories, invitations, shopping list, shared notes (title, content, who wrote them, whether they are sensitive, and the 20 previous versions of each), important dates (title, day, month and optional year; they may concern relatives, such as a birthday).
Guest link (if a member creates one): a secret link opens the shopping list only (items, quantities, aisles and the household name), read-only and with no account, until a member turns it off or replaces it. Anyone with the link can see it.
Tasks: titles, notes, dates, times, durations, assignees, recurrences, status, sub-tasks, comments, turn-swap requests (with any note), declared absences, activity history (who did what, when).
Expenses (if you use them): amount, date, label, category, comment, who paid and each person's share. A personal expense is visible to you only. An attached receipt (photo or PDF) is kept with the expense and deleted with it. If you use “Read a receipt”, the photo is read on our server (no outside service) to suggest the amount, date and shop, then deleted straight away; it is only kept if you save the expense with that receipt.
Sessions: device (browser and system, or Android app version), sign-in date and last activity, shown in “Signed-in devices” so you can sign out remotely. Android app: the phone's notification identifier (if instant notifications are enabled), deleted when you sign out.
The Android app keeps a copy of your tasks, shopping list, notes and important dates on the phone to work offline; it is erased when you sign out.
Add by e-mail (if you turn it on): the sender, subject and text of e-mails you forward to your personal address are saved in the notes of the task created. They are received by Resend, our e-mail provider; their attachments are added to the task.
Attachments: files you attach to a task (or attached to a forwarded e-mail) are stored on our server with the task, visible to household members (only to you for a personal task), and deleted with it.
Reports (if you send any): the type, title and text of your message, a screenshot if you attach one, whether you agree to be contacted and, only if you tick the box, technical information shown before sending (browser or phone model, system, app version, language, time zone, screen size, open page). Never the content of your tasks. Only the app's administrators read them.
Browser notifications (if you turn them on): the subscription address provided by your browser, deleted when you turn them off or sign out.

google.title: Google data
google.body:
Sign in with Google: the app receives your Google identifier and verified email address, only to sign you in. The app never sees your Google password.
Google Calendar (if you connect it): the app reads the list of your calendars (so you can pick the shared calendar) and only creates, updates or deletes the events it created itself for your tasks. It does not read your other events. Google access tokens are encrypted (AES-256-GCM) on the server and revoked when you disconnect or delete your account.
The app's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements: this data is not transferred to third parties, not used for advertising, and not read by humans except at your request to fix a problem or when required by law.

use.title: Why
use.body: To show and share household tasks, send reminders, sync the shared calendar if you enable it, let you reset your password by email, and diagnose technical errors. Legal basis: providing the service you use and, for Google Calendar, your consent (which you can withdraw at any time).

processors.title: Service providers
processors.body: Cloudflare (site delivery and protection), Google (if you use Google sign-in or Google Calendar), the email provider configured for “forgot password” (e.g. Brevo), off-site backup storage if configured (e.g. Cloudflare R2), Google Firebase Cloud Messaging for instant notifications in the Android app if enabled (it only receives the phone's notification identifier and a “something new” signal, never task content or names), browsers' push services (Google, Mozilla, Apple) if you turn on site notifications (messages pass through them encrypted, unreadable to them), and, if enabled, an error-tracking service (Sentry) that only receives technical information (error type, page), without task content or identity.

retention.title: Retention
retention.body:
Your data is kept as long as your account exists. A deleted task stays in the household's trash for 30 days, then is permanently erased. The activity log (who did what, and when) is kept for one year. Sessions expire after 60 days of inactivity. Password reset links expire after 30 minutes. A report is kept while open, then 180 days after it is resolved (you can withdraw it at any time).
Account deletion: immediate in the app. Backups are kept 14 days on the server and 30 days off-site: your data disappears from them at the latest after that.

security.title: Security
security.body: Encrypted connections (HTTPS), hashed passwords, encrypted Google tokens, strict separation between households, personal tasks visible only to you, sign-in attempt limits, verified daily backups.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: From Settings → Data & privacy you can at any time: export all your data (JSON file), unlink Google, disconnect Google Calendar, delete your account. From Settings → Help → Report a problem, you can withdraw your reports. You also have the rights of access, rectification, objection and complaint to your country's data protection authority.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body:
Only strictly necessary cookies: sign-in session (httpOnly, secure) and, for a few minutes, tracking of a Google sign-in in progress. Your light/dark theme choice is stored in your browser. No analytics or advertising cookies.
Offline: the site keeps in your browser (local storage and service worker cache) a copy of the household data already displayed, so it stays usable without a network. It is erased when you sign out.

about.metaTitle: Tandem · The perfect balance for your household
about.tagline: The perfect balance for your household.
about.intro: Tandem is a private app that helps a household share its chores: who takes out the bins, who does the shopping, who calls the garage. It is available as a website and an Android app.
about.features:
A "Today" list: overdue, today, this week.
Natural-language quick add ("Take out the bins tomorrow 7pm"), by voice too.
Recurring tasks with turn-taking between household members.
Shared shopping list, updated in real time.
Reminders, and notifications when someone assigns you a task.
Works offline, on the website and in the Android app.
about.googleTitle: Why the app asks for access to Google
about.google:
Sign in with Google (optional): to sign in without a password. The app only receives your name, email address and Google identifier.
Google Calendar (optional): so that household tasks appear in a shared Google calendar on all your devices. The app reads your list of calendars so you can pick the shared one, then creates, updates and deletes only the events that correspond to your tasks. It does not read your other events.
Data received from Google is never sold, shared or used for advertising.
about.footer: A personal app, free and ad-free.
